newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indian wheat buyers out for next six months-USDA.
newsitem.headline: Indian wheat buyers out for next six months-USDA.

text.p: India will probably not enter the wheat market in 1997 but may consider imports in early 1998, a senior U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) economist said on Thursday.
"At least for the next six months, (India will) be able to stay out of the market," the USDA economist told Reuters in an interview at a wheat conference in Singapore.
"For the time being, it appears they have a good harvest," he said. "By next spring, they'll have a little better idea what their next harvest will be looking like."
The U.S. agricultural counselor in New Delhi, Thomas Pomeroy, said in an interview on Wednesday that India may have to import 1.0-2.0 million tonnes of wheat.
"There's a possibility they might buy a million or two more tonnes, but I don't think they're going to do it for several months," Pomeroy said.

In India, analysts and traders said on Thursday lower domestic prices, timely imports and comfortable stocks make it unlikely that New Delhi would look for more imports in the 1997/98 (April/March) fiscal year.
The Indian government has estimated the domestic wheat crop at 68.71 million tonnes in the 1996/97 (June/July) crop year against the previous season's 62.62 million tonnes.
